title.justification: The title is directly extracted from the research paper as mentioned at the start of the text.

analysis.description: The paper addresses the challenge of learning temporal abstractions that can be reused in different tasks. It focuses on the use of interest functions in the options framework, aiming to make these temporal abstractions, or options, more specialized and meaningful by proposing new theorems within the option-critic architecture.

type.justification: The paper presents a theoretical framework by introducing new theorems for the use of interest functions in the options framework.
type.quote: We build on the option-critic framework (Bacon, Harb, and Precup 2017) to derive policy gradient theorems for interest functions leading to a new interest-option-critic architecture.

name.justification: The focus of the paper is on the reinforcement learning framework, specifically addressing temporal abstractions and the options framework.
name.quote: The work, we tackle this problem in the options framework (Sutton, Precup, and Singh 1999; Precup 2000).

name.justification: The paper addresses the issue of learning temporal abstractions through the use of options and interest functions within the reinforcement learning framework.
name.quote: Learning temporal abstractions which are partial solutions to a task and could be reused for solving other tasks is an ingredient that can help agents to plan and learn efficiently.

name.justification: The research involves deriving policy gradient theorems for interest functions, which are a part of the reinforcement learning methodologies.
name.quote: We build on the option-critic framework (Bacon, Harb, and Precup 2017) to derive policy gradient theorems for interest functions.

name.justification: The paper introduces a new architecture called the interest-option-critic, which incorporates interest functions into the option-critic framework.
name.quote: We build on the option-critic framework (Bacon, Harb, and Precup 2017) to derive policy gradient theorems for interest functions leading to a new interest-option-critic architecture.
